phrase: my kid lands a skateboard trick and I want it to look like a skate video

spec.movement: locked: the camera does not move, the action comes to it
spec.placement: on the floor, 3 m away, the lens level and looking along the ground into the light
spec.lens_why: An ultra-wide lens on the floor makes the ground rush to the lens and gives a small jump real scale.
risks: Do not tilt the lens up at the face: it bends bodies and generators stretch them. Keep the lens level.
Slow motion plus a jump invites floating. Write a real height and real gravity.

one_line: A kid on a skateboard landing a kickflip off a low kerb, seen from a locked camera on the floor with an ultra-wide lens, the lens level, looking along the ground into the light; 18 mm lens; flat overcast daylight from a grey sky, soft contact shadows under bodies and objects, muted natural contrast, no sun; muted earth-tone grade: browns, greys and dull greens, low saturation, soft highlights, worn surfaces; slow motion for this one beat only; real gravity, weight and cloth move truthfully, nothing floats; an extremely wide lens very low and very close to the wheels, the ground rushing past the bottom of the frame, lines bending at the edges, plain daylight. Avoid: not a default eye-level medium shot; no soft even glow; one motivated light source with a real dark side; nobody looks into the lens; every eyeline goes to a target inside the scene; no slow floating camera drift; the camera is locked or makes one decisive move with a clear end; real gravity and real jump height, nobody floats; no bloom, no haze, no fog, no volumetric god rays.
